record.what_it_does: Team chat and messaging app (CAKE.com) with channels, DMs and apps.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization-code flow (consent at app.pumble.com/access-request, token exchange at api-ga.pumble.com/oauth2/access). It returns a user accessToken and a botToken, and these do not need refreshing. Requests send x-app-token and token headers. There is also a per-user API key via the "API keys" add-on, limited to 1000 requests/min/user. That add-on is simpler but is not suited to multi-user use.
record.access_notes: The API key add-on is stated as available on all plans. Apps are created with a manifest through pumble-cli or the API. I found no evidence that building apps needs a paid plan. Whether installing in other workspaces, or listing on the CAKE.com Marketplace, needs review is unconfirmed.
record.api_breadth_notes: The SDK ApiClient has about 40 methods: messages (post, DM, reply, edit, delete, reactions, search, scheduled, drafts, ephemeral), channels, users, user groups, profile, status, workspace info, files, calls and app home view. The API key add-on exposes a smaller Swagger-documented set.
record.mcp_notes: No MCP server turned up in my searches. I did not search specifically for community MCP servers.
record.blocker_notes: The OAuth flow, scopes and eventSubscriptions are documented, so a public OAuth app looks workable. The caveats are that the docs I found are only on the SDK site (cake-com.github.io). The marketplace publishing and review requirements are unverified. The Swagger spec I saw referenced covers only the API-key add-on, and I did not open it.

evidence.quote: Every Request to Pumble API must be sent with two headers.
Each ApiClient method has its own set of required scopes.

record.needs_human: Check: (1) whether apps can be installed in other workspaces without Marketplace review, and what the "Publishing to CAKE.com Marketplace" guide requires; (2) whether the Swagger/OpenAPI spec is public; (3) whether a sandbox exists; (4) whether any official or community MCP server exists. The SDK docs sit on cake-com.github.io, which looks CAKE.com-owned but is unconfirmed. The openapi_spec value applies only to the API-key add-on.
